about: Question design for the Assignment 02 pilot (ECE 2514). Main questions are predict and tracing only, one per function, the type rotating by form. After a correct main answer the student gets a fixed follow-up per function (see fixedFollowUps). Fields "spec" (predict answers) and "refStops" (the reference's trace stops, used only to choose a K for targeted inputs) are filled by run-all.js by running code. Do not edit them by hand. There is no spec answer for tracing: the answer is the student's own trace.
placeholders: Main questions: {input} = the input's "display" text; tracing also {line} (the student's breakpoint line, pauseLine in meta.json), {function}, {kth} ("1st", "2nd", ..., chosen per student from their own trace) and {what} (per function, tracing.what).
tracingQuestion: You put a breakpoint on line {line} and run {function} on {input}. When it stops for the {kth} time, {what}?
compileErrorQuestion: Your {function} doesn't compile. The compiler points to line {line}. What is wrong on that line, and how would you fix it?
compileErrorOutsideQuestion: Your code doesn't compile. The compiler points to line {line}. What is wrong on that line, and how would you fix it?
logicQuestion: Walk me through what your {function} would do with {input}, step by step.
backup: mode is the backup. It replaces a function that cannot be asked (for example a tracing question when the function has no line to put a breakpoint on) and takes the type of the function it replaces.

fixedFollowUps.note: The same question and the same answer key for every student, no code run. Asked only after a correct main answer (the engine rule is M4b). Stored in the plan as fixedFollowUp. Compile-error and logic questions have none.

reverseList.question: Why does reversing in place only need to go through half of the vector? What would happen if the swapping continued all the way to the end?
reverseList.answerKey: Each swap places two numbers; going all the way swaps everything back, so the vector ends up unchanged.

splitString.question: Why does splitting "apple,banana,orange" with '|' give one piece instead of none?
splitString.answerKey: There is no delimiter, so the whole string is the one piece.

playCraps.question: Why does {4, 3} end the game right away, but {2, 2} needs more rolls?
playCraps.answerKey: 7 on the first roll is an instant win; 4 becomes the number to roll again.

mode.question: In {3, 1, 3, 1} both numbers appear twice. Which one should mode return, and why?
mode.answerKey: 1, because a tie goes to the smallest number.

inputRules: An input where the code crashes, gives a runtime error or hits the time limit is never used (undefined behavior). The next separating input is used; if none, a standard input with targeted = false.

playCraps inputs whose answer depends on the validation reading in SPEC-NOTES.md (an invalid value after the game is already decided) have unclearSpec = true and are not used until the spec is confirmed.
Inputs that end with a delimiter, and playCraps inputs with an odd number of values, are never used (not defined by the spec).
